By submitting your Recordings to Afrobeats Africa, you acknowledge and grant us the right to synchronize ("Sync Rights") your Recordings with visual images and to allow Digital Stores and their users to use these Sync Rights, including any necessary rights of performance and reproduction required for the operation of such Digital Stores.

Furthermore, the rights granted to Afrobeats Africa under this Agreement the right to grant, administer, and collect under "micro" sync licenses, as that term is understood in the music publishing industry. "Micro" syncs include blanket licenses for the use of Compositions (or portions thereof, including lyrics or metadata) in various types of multimedia projects such as videos, slideshows, presentations, social media platforms, software apps, and on video sites and services such as YouTube, Vevo, and Vimeo.

Regarding YouTube, Afrobeats Africa' rights include the right to identify, "claim," and "monetize" videos containing your Compositions by allowing the display of advertising. * To create "art tracks" using your recordings, create reference files and fingerprints of your recordings, and use your recordings in Facebook properties that include musical emojis/stickers, video re-mix, send-a-lyric, virtual reality experiences, singalong with lyrics.  
* To display and use your Licensor(s), Artist(s), Author(s), Stage name, Persona, band name and/or label name and logo (if you have one), all artwork, song and album titles, all trademarks, service marks, logos and trade names, and all Licensor, songwriter, producer and mixer names and approved likenesses, as embodied in metadata within the recordings or otherwise provided by you ("Materials"), on Afrobeats Africa Sites, on the Digital Stores' sites and services, and in any marketing, advertising or promotional materials for our Service or for the Digital Stores.

# ROYALTIES AND COMMISSIONS

We offer Music Distribution as a free service, which means that there are no fees associated with distributing your music to digital stores. Please note that we collect a percentage of the royalties that are collected on your behalf. These royalties are split with 75% going to the Licensor and 25% in the form of commission to Afrobeats Africa. For more information on how this commission is calculated, please refer to the "Royalties" section.

Our Commission Fee of twenty percent (25%) includes commission on performances, sync licensing, merchandise, streaming, and music publishing. We will be heavily involved in the marketing of performances moving forward, providing not only promotion services, press releases, live streaming of some performance events, and graphic design services, but also requiring the use of a ticketing system to provide accurate financial reporting and capture attendees' cell phone and email, which can be used for marketing future performances.

## COMMISSION ON LITERARY WORKS

Afrobeats Africa will receive a commission of 25% on the net revenue from the sale of any books or literary Works derived from or related to the Licensor's original Work. This commission will also apply to any other use of the Licensor's Work, including but not limited to translations, adaptations, and licensed derivatives.

The commission will be deducted from the gross revenue generated by the sale or use of the Licensor's Work, and the net revenue will be shared with the Licensor on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

## TICKET SALES

The Company shall receive 25% of all ticket sales for live performances of the Works, regardless of the promoter. As the Company will be the primary marketer of the Works, its work will directly impact ticket sales. The promoter shall receive 15% of all ticket sales for live performances of the Works. The remaining 60% of all ticket sales shall be paid to the Licensor.

In the case of ticket sales, all expenses, fees, and charges will be deducted from total gross ticket sales before any commission splits are made. The Licensor is responsible for paying any and all expenses incurred in connection with the performance of the Services, including, but not limited to, travel expenses, lodging expenses, and meal expenses.

For miscellaneous income sources, including but not limited to monies from YouTube ads and social media sites, commissions will be paid after all applicable fees, expenses, charges, and deductions are made from the gross revenue.

Commission payments will be made within 30 days of the receipt of funds by the Company. The Company shall provide the Licensor with a detailed statement of all revenues and expenses relating to the Licensor's activities and the distribution of the Licensor's materials.

## ACCEPTANCE OF COMMISSIONS

The Licensor acknowledges and agrees that this commission is fair and reasonable, and is necessary to compensate Afrobeats Africa for its efforts in promoting, marketing, and distributing the Licensor's Work to the widest possible audience. By entering into this Agreement, the Licensor authorizes Afrobeats Africa to deduct this commission from any revenue generated by the sale or use of their literary Works, and to remit the remaining net revenue to the Licensor on a timely basis.

Afrobeats Africa is committed to maximizing the royalties earned by our licenses through our music distribution services. We work diligently to ensure that all royalties owed to our Licensor are collected and distributed in a timely and accurate manner. 

 Afrobeats Africa is not a collecting society or performing rights organization. We are able to publish music through ASCAP, CAPASSO and Sound Exchange. While we will make reasonable efforts to collect and distribute royalty payments for your music, we cannot guarantee or promise any revenue or specific results from the use of our Services. Afrobeats Africa cannot and does not make any guarantees about your ability to get results or earn any money from our services, ideas, information, training, tools, or strategies through our third-party contacts.

This includes countries like Gambia and others with similar situations. Upon termination of this Agreement, we may withhold all Royalties due for a period of time permitted by applicable law from the date they would otherwise be payable in order to ensure our ability to offset any refunds or other offsets we are entitled to take against the Royalties.

If we terminate this Agreement because you have breached your representations and warranties, you forfeit all Royalties not yet paid to you.

If we determine in our sole discretion that deceptive, fraudulent, or illegal activity has occurred with respect to your Works, then we may permanently withhold payments to you, and we may offset any payments previously paid against future payments or require you to remit them to us. # ADDICTION RECOVERY

The Company is committed to providing support and understanding to individuals who are in recovery for addiction. We do not discriminate against anyone based on their addiction recovery status. This means that we will not terminate this agreement or seek to alter its terms solely on the grounds of being in recovery for addiction. We firmly believe in the power of addiction recovery programs and the potential for individuals with addiction to achieve success. If you are currently struggling with addiction, we strongly encourage you to seek help. The Company is here to assist and support you on your journey to recovery by offering recommendations for treatment programs, support groups, and counseling services. We recognize our role in helping those in recovery and are dedicated to fostering an environment that supports your commitment to sobriety and allows you to continue your work as an Artist.

We also understand the importance of maintaining a safe and professional environment for all involved parties. Therefore, the following objective criteria may trigger drug testing for artists in recovery:

* **Unexplained absences**: If the artist has unexplained absences from scheduled performances or events without a valid reason, it may trigger a drug test requirement.  
* **Impaired performance**: If the artist's performance is noticeably impaired, affecting their ability to deliver their artistic content or fulfill their obligations under the agreement, it may warrant drug testing.  
* **Public safety concerns**: If there are concerns about the artist's behavior, demeanor, or actions that pose a risk to their safety, the safety of others, or the reputation of the company, drug testing may be required.  
* **Legal involvement**: If the artist becomes involved in legal issues related to substance abuse or if law enforcement is involved in any incidents, it may trigger drug testing.

Health and safety regulations: If there are specific health and safety regulations in the industry or the venues where the artist performs that require drug testing for all participants, compliance with these regulations can be a criterion.

The Company acknowledges its role in helping those in recovery and is willing to assist artists in seeking recovery, including recommending treatment programs, support groups, and counseling services. By being supportive and understanding, we aim to help artists maintain their commitment to sobriety and continue their work as performers.

For the safety of all individuals associated with The Company, including employees, vendors, partners, and the public, drug testing may be requested in the following circumstances: during performances, events, appearances, interviews, when out in public, or when law enforcement is involved. Additionally, random drug testing may be required for artists in recovery, and compliance with other policies designed to ensure safety may be necessary.

Please note that these drug testing provisions are solely intended to ensure a safe and professional working environment and are not intended to discriminate against individuals in recovery. The Company remains committed to treating all artists fairly and in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

# APPENDIX A

## STEPS TO GETTING PAID

Appendix A, which outlines the steps required to receive payment from Afrobeats Africa. Here is a summary of each step:

1. **Provide your tax information**: Depending on your location, Afrobeats Africa may need to collect tax-related information from you. All Licensors receiving payment over $50 USD from Afrobeats Africa, regardless of their location in the world, are required to provide tax information.

2. **Confirm your personal information**: It's important to confirm the accuracy of your payment name and address so that Afrobeats Africa can verify your identity and send you a Personal Identification Number (PIN). If you need to correct any information, you can follow the instructions provided by Afrobeats Africa.

3. **Verify your identity**: To continue receiving royalty payments from Afrobeats Africa, you need to verify your identity. This is to confirm the accuracy of your account information and protect you from fraud, as well as comply with U.S. Federal Regulations.

4. **Select your form of payment**: When your earnings reach the payment method selection threshold, you can select your preferred form of payment. Depending on your payment address, there may be several forms of payment available to you, including Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) and wire transfer.

5. **Meet the payment threshold**: If your current balance reaches the payment threshold of $10 by the end of the month, a 21-day payment processing period begins. After the processing period ends, Afrobeats Africa will issue you a payment.
